column1: # ryo-v2 fork: every `unsafe` the fork patch (D11) adds to the vendored salsa, site by site, with its reasoning. Upstream's own `unsafe` is not listed; a site the patch only moved or re-signed is listed as such.

column4: classification
column5: SAFETY

column4: moved: upstream's `Zalsa::memo_table_for`, unchanged
column5: the base's own current revision is passed, as upstream does; only the branch without a layer reaches it
column7: moved from src/zalsa.rs so that a layered handle cannot reach it

column4: new: a type-erased handle of a memo a layer holds
column5: the pointer is the base address of a whole boxed `Memo<C>` (the layer boxes each memo and frees it only when the layer drops, after every borrow of the layer); `to_dyn_fn` and `TypeId` are those of `Memo<C>`, the type the downcast just checked

column4: new: copy of upstream's `get_memo_from_table_for` for the base
column5: the base's own current revision is passed; serialization holds exclusive access, so the memo stays allocated for `'db`, as upstream argues for `get_memo_from_table_for`

column4: re-bound: upstream's block, its value now named `base`
column5: unchanged reasoning: memos are freed only at a new revision, which a frozen base does not reach

column4: new: upstream's `intern_id` and `intern_id_cold` steps without the LRU, durability and revision-queue writes
column5: each block is the same call under the same condition as in upstream's `intern_id`/`intern_id_cold`: the shard index comes from `self.shard`, the shard lock is held for every value access (the lookup's owner check reads an atomic under it), the value was allocated through this ingredient's memo types and is inserted under its shard's lock
column7: no base slot is reused (E7); a value is seen only by its owner's chain; new values are immortal and never enter the LRU; a slot a dropped layer gave back is taken again in `reuse_in_layer`

column4: new: trait method
column5: the caller passes an initialized slot of a frozen base, which neither reuses nor deletes it, so `memos_unchecked`'s condition holds

column3: unsafe block (`mem::transmute` of `T::memos_in_layer`) and a block dereferencing the slot pointer in `fork_fingerprint`
column4: new: two vtable entries
column5: the transmute is the same ABI-compatible erasure upstream uses for `memos_unchecked`; the fingerprint closure is only called with a pointer to an initialized slot of the page's type

column4: new: upstream's `dyn_memos_unchecked` with the layer check
column5: `Page::get` checks initialization; the base is frozen while a layer lives; the page keeps the right memo types

column4: new: the isolation readout (I2)
column5: every slot pointer comes from `Page::get` below both `allocated` and the page's `allocated` at the freeze (`fork_allocated`); the only caller, `fork::base_fingerprint`, panics unless the base is frozen, so no slot read is reused or deleted, no non-atomic field of it is written, and no memo is inserted, replaced or freed during the traversal: layer queries meanwhile make only atomic stores to such slots; the slots a layer allocates or takes again under this freeze are above the freeze's counts, except interned slots a layer of an earlier freeze owned, which a layer of this one may take again: the vtable's `fork_fingerprint` reads their owner with one atomic load and returns `false` before anything else is read, and their memo table is then not touched
column7: read-only; the frozen check was added in review: on a base that takes writes, a query on another handle writes a tracked struct's plain `durability` field in `update`, a data race with this read; the freeze-time counts and the owner skip came with the freeing of layer-owned slots

column4: new: read-only traversal of a base slot's memos
column5: `insert` type-checks and release-publishes each pointer with its entry type; the slot belongs to a frozen base, which frees no memo for `'a`
column7: used when a layer tombstones a struct

column4: new: the isolation readout (I2)
column5: as `get_erased`: the pointer and its entry type were published together by `insert`; the caller (`Table::fork_fingerprint`, reached only through `fork::base_fingerprint` on a frozen base) keeps the memos alive: a frozen base frees no memo

column3: unsafe block (`transmute` of a field reference's lifetime)
column4: new: upstream's `lock_fields` lifetime restoration
column5: guaranteed by `Configuration`; the restored lifetime is bounded by the borrow of the retained fields (a layer's entry or a frozen base slot)

column3: unsafe blocks (load of `updated_at`, `&*data`, `transmute` of the new fields to `'static`)
column4: new: the re-creation of a struct under a layer
column5: `data` comes from `data_raw` of a live id; `updated_at` is never exclusively borrowed; the frozen base does not write the slot, and a slot a layer owns is written only when it is taken again, after every layer that could name its id has dropped, so a shared reference to it is sound; the transmute is upstream's `allocate` retention, the fields kept only in the layer's entry
column7: the base slot is read, never written

column3: unsafe blocks (`transmute` of the fields, `MemoTable::new`, `&mut *data_raw` of a slot taken again)
column4: new: upstream's `allocate` with a layer free list instead of the base's
column5: the transmute and `MemoTable::new` as upstream's `allocate`; the `&mut` is upstream's free-list reuse (`*data_raw = value(id)`) of a slot a dropped layer of this freeze gave back: only that layer's chain reached it and every layer of the chain has dropped, so no reference to it is alive; the pop hands it to this call only; it lies above the freeze's `allocated` counts, so the base fingerprint does not read it; the old contents are dropped by the assignment (the memo table is empty: a layer inserts no memo into a slot's table)
column7: a slot of an earlier freeze, or whose generation cannot be bumped, is leaked (counted), never written

column4: new: at a thaw, the layer free list moves to the base's free list
column5: the table is borrowed exclusively (`&mut Table`, from `try_thaw`'s `&mut Zalsa`); every slot on the layer free list was given back by a dropped layer, so no reference to it is alive; `updated_at` is set to `None`, the state `delete_entity` leaves for the base's free list
column7: the base then reuses the slot by upstream's `allocate`

column3: unsafe blocks (`value_hash` in the hasher closure and on the dead value, `mem::replace` of the fields `UnsafeCell`, the id `UnsafeCell`)
column4: new: a slot a dropped layer gave back taken again under a layer
column5: the caller holds the lock of the slot's shard (its free list is per shard and the shard is fixed), which guards the fields, the id and the key map; the slot was owned by a dropped layer: the lookup matches a value only for its owner's chain and every layer of that chain has dropped, so no reference to its fields or memos is alive and no lookup can return it meanwhile; its old key-map entry is removed before the fields change and a new one inserted after; it is immortal (never in the LRU) and its memo table is empty; the base fingerprint skips it by its owner (atomic)
column7: upstream's stale-slot reuse in `intern_id`, with ownership in place of the LRU's staleness; the generation is bumped for a reusable ingredient, and kept for an immortal one (upstream never moves it; rust-analyzer rebuilds `SyntaxContext` ids from the bare index), which ownership makes sound: no holder of the old value is alive

column4: new: at a thaw, every layer-owned value leaves the key maps
column5: the shards are borrowed exclusively (`&mut self`); every key-map pointer is to a live value of the table, which keeps it until the ingredient drops; only the atomic owner is read
column7: so the base's lookup, which has no owner check, never returns a layer's value

column4: new: the read of a base struct under a layer
column5: `updated_at` is never exclusively borrowed

column4: new
column5: `data` is a live slot whose `updated_at` was just found `Some`; the frozen base does not write its fields or revisions

column4: new: override that checks `updated_at` without taking the read lock
column5: the caller passes a valid slot; the frozen base neither deletes nor reuses it
